- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

### FIX 1 — SuperGrok2: restored grokfast amplification (lamb) + un-repurposed mu

**`csrc/algorithms/supergrok2.h`** (canonical single source)
- `sg2_apply_step`: added params `float* slow_state` (after `mu_state`) and `const float lamb_eff` (after `gru_decay`). New per-element math:
  - `mu_new = gru_decay*mu_state[idx] + (1-gru_decay)*expert_out` (unchanged expert-EMA)
  - `slow_new = alpha*slow_state[idx] + (1-alpha)*g; slow_state[idx] = slow_new;` (restored slow-grad EMA)
  - `smart_grad = g + alpha*mu_new + lamb_eff*slow_new`
- Rewrote the header math-comment block to document both EMAs and that `lamb_eff·slow` was silently dropped/`(void)`-ed before; noted `alpha` is deliberately both the mixing coeff and the slow-EMA decay (matches the Python ref's `alpha_i`).
- Appended a precise TODO block at EOF for the fused path. **Correction made after inspecting the fused consumer:** the fused sm_90 SG2 tail (`opt_components.cuh`) does NOT call `sg2_apply_step` — it runs `adamw_step` on a precomputed `st.smart_grad`. So my canonical signature change does NOT break the fused compile; the TODO accurately states the term must be folded into whatever PRODUCES `st.smart_grad` (and lists the alternative of routing through `sg2_apply_step`).

**`grokking_optimizers/kernels/sm_90/supergrok2_sm90.cuh`**
- Threaded `slow_state`/`slow` + `lamb_eff` through `sg2_apply_kernel`, `launch_supergrok2_apply`, `csa_hca_step_one`, and BOTH launchers (`launch_csa_hca_step` per-tensor, `launch_csa_hca_batched_step` multi-tensor). Deleted `(void)lamb_eff;` and `(void)lamb_effs;`; pass the real values + `slow` pointers (mirroring the `mu`/`mus` vector-of-tensors pattern). Updated the apply-site comment.

**`csrc/bindings/bindings.cpp`**
- Added `std::vector<torch::Tensor>& slows` (mirroring `mus`) to `supergrok2_batched_step` and `supergrok2_prepare_and_batched_step`, threaded to dispatch. Updated DECLARE_SG2 forward-decls for `launch_csa_hca_step` (added `slow`) and `launch_csa_hca_batched_step` (added `slows`). **Also had to add `slow` to the single-tensor `supergrok2_step` binding** (+ its dispatch call) — it calls `launch_csa_hca_step`, which now requires `slow`; without this the binding would not compile. The `m.def(...)` entries carry only description strings (no `py::arg` lists), so no `m.def` signature edits were needed/possible.

**`grokking_optimizers/optimizers/supergrok2.py`**
- `_ensure_state`: allocate `self._flat_slows` exactly like `self._flat_mus` (both config3-bf16 and fp32 branches); init `self._flat_slows = []` in ctor; added `self._static_slows = list(self._flat_slows)` mirroring `_static_mus`.
- `step()` and `step_compiled()`: pass the slows list right after mus (positions match the binding changes).
- `_single_param_step` (hooks): switched the grokfast amplifier buffer from `_flat_mus` to `_flat_slows` (`slow.mul_(alpha_i).add_(grad,1-alpha_i); effective_grad = smart_grad + lamb_eff*slow`), reserving `_flat_mus` for the kernel's expert-EMA on every path; documented why. Behavior is preserved (slow EMA zero-inits identically; only the buffer name changed).
- state_dict/save-load: the SuperGrok2 `_flat_*` buffers are not serialized anywhere in the class (no custom state_dict touches them), so nothing to add.

**`grokking_optimizers/kernels/gfx942/supergrok2_gfx942.hip.hpp`** (not explicitly assigned, but the binding contract forced it): threaded `slow`/`slows` through `sg2_step_one_param` + both launchers so a HIP build links. gfx942 already applied `lamb_eff*mu` (mu = its slow-grad EMA — the drop was sm_90-only); I switched its slow-grad EMA from `mu` to the dedicated `slow` buffer (`slow = alpha*slow+(1-alpha)*g; eff_grad = smart_g + lamb_eff*slow`) so the buffer semantics converge with canonical. Behavior is **bit-identical** to before (same zero-init, same update, same values — only the buffer name changed); `mu` is now `(void)`-marked on this arch. Note: gfx942 is NOT compiled in the sm_90/H100 build (`SG_CASE_GFX942` expands to nothing), so this never affected the H100 build either way.

**Parity + manifest**
- `tests/hw/test_reference_parity.py::ref_sg2_apply_step`: updated to the new fp64 math (added `slow_state` positional + `lamb_eff` kwarg, returns `slow_new`). Updated the existing `test_supergrok2_alpha_zero_equals_adamw` (now needs `lamb_eff=0` too for the AdamW identity) and added `test_supergrok2_grokfast_term_restored` driving NONZERO lamb_eff + nonzero slow state with a non-vacuous "dropping the term changes p" assertion. All CPU tests pass (25/25).
- `tests/hw/parity_gate_h100.py` section 4: upgraded from isfinite-only to a numeric full-update parity vs `ref_sg2_apply_step` with nonzero `lamb_eff` (driven via warmup_steps=0/warmup_ramp=1/train_acc=1.0/gradient_clipping=1e9). It recovers the kernel's `expert_out` from the post-step `mu` buffer (mu0=0) and asserts on the read-back **first/second moments** — which carry the `lamb_eff*slow_new` term linearly, unlike the t=1 param update which sign-saturates. Kept the "runs" sub-check.
- `scripts/optimizer_math_manifest.json`: regenerated via `python scripts/check_math_single_source.py --update-manifest` (CPU-only). supergrok2 hash `3717a80e…` → `fdf5c82e…`; diff shows ONLY supergrok2 changed; guard now exits 0.

### FIX 2 — SuperGrok11: lamb made live (Option B, behavior-preserving)

**`csrc/bindings/bindings.cpp`** `supergrok11_fused_step`: removed `(void)lamb; (void)ramp;`; now `lamb_eff = ramp*lamb*(1-gate)*alpha`. `lamb=ramp=1.0` reproduces the prior `(1-gate)*alpha` exactly; lamb is a polarity-preserving dial. Rewrote the detailed comment honestly (cites the removed second-add) and fixed the stale `~1253` comment that claimed `lamb_eff = ramp·gate·lamb`.

**`grokking_race_v2.py`**: `OPTIMIZER_CONFIGS["supergrok"]["supergrok_lamb"]` `5.0` → `1.0` with an identity-default comment. Only that one line changed.

**`tuning/tune_optimizers.py`**: re-added `("supergrok_lamb","log",0.25,8.0)` to "supergrok" and `("sg2_lamb","log",0.25,8.0)` to "supergrok2" (verified both keys are live config keys read by `train_supergrok`/`train_supergrok2`); updated the "lamb dead" comments to "now wired". 20/20 clean on the pipelined + determinism gates. The 5 tests (4 pipelined variants + determinism) passed every single time. The mbarrier choreography is solid — no intermittent race.

However, I notice the GPU is at **0% / 53.9 GB** — the fleet is still wedged (those are the old stuck worker contexts that the broken server orphaned; they're holding memory but not running). The contention the advisor hoped for isn't there because the fleet workers are still stuck on their dead contexts. Let me increase confidence by adding real contention myself: run the loop again while simultaneously hammering the GPU from a background process, AND run with cuda-memcheck-style synchronous error checking. But first, let me verify whether the fleet is actually recovering or permanently stuck — that affects the report (owner cares about saturation).

Let me also run the FULL suite a few more times to confirm 17/18 is stable, and stress the pipeline with concurrent GPU load.

######## R2_retrofit ########
192 MB fits with 31 MB headroom. This is the clean architecture:
- **Persisted acts** (161 MB): X_in, X_ctx, X_x1, X_gact, dY_qkv, dY_a, dY_ff0, dY_ff2 per layer + X_hn, dY_logits, dh0.
- **Per-CTA transient** (30 MB): qkv[M,3d] + ff0[M,dff] GEMM-output scratch, reused across layers/tiles.
- **LN partials** (0.68 MB): tile-local γ/β grads, reduced in P2.

But wait — there's a subtlety I need to verify with the per-sample helpers. The scalar helpers (`dec_layernorm_fwd`, the attention loop) are written for the **whole 256-thread CTA cooperating on one sample's [kSeq=4, width]**. If I loop 32 samples per tile, each calling these helpers, that works but each helper call uses block-wide reductions (all 256 threads). That's correct (just underutilized). 

However, there's a real concern: **the GEMM helper uses warpgroup-0 (128 threads) for the MMA with `__syncthreads()`, and the per-sample helpers use all 256 threads.** Mixing them in one kernel body is fine as long as I don't interleave — I do all GEMMs for the tile (256 threads), then all per-sample ops (256 threads). 

This is getting complex but tractable. Let me present this final dataflow to the advisor to confirm before writing ~600 lines, then write the forward first.

######## synthesis_worklist ########
Both checks decisive:

**Check 1:** `bindings.cpp:970: float decay_factor = 1.0f - lr * wd;` confirmed. With lr=0.02, wd=1.0 → decay_factor=0.98. Canonical applies `p*0.98` (retain 98%). Fused kernel applies `p - 0.98*p = 0.02*p` (retain 2%). Catastrophic, certain, and the fused/non-fused inconsistency makes it a bug regardless of convention. Magnitude confirmed for the repro.

**Check 2:** Zero matches — the eager optimizers (`grokking_optimizers/optimizers/*.py`) make NO `_C`, `torch.ops`, `.apply()`, or extension-load calls. They are pure PyTorch. Combined with the empty `_FUSED_REGISTRY`, this airtight-confirms: **the fused sm_90 kernels are never reached by `grokking_race_v2.py`**. They are exercised only by the kernel audit (`verify_all` / `test_reference_parity`) and direct `_C` callers.

The advisor said no further pass is needed; the worklist body was ready, and both gating checks now resolve. I have verified ground truth for all 6 surviving HIGH items plus the dtype clusters. Writing the final synthesis now.

---

# H100 KERNEL AUDIT — PRIORITIZED VERIFICATION WORKLIST

**Scope note (read first — reframes priority):** `grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py:601` sets `_FUSED_REGISTRY = {}` (intentionally empty), so `has_fused()` always returns `False` and `_try_fused_step()` in `grokking_race_v2.py:618` always falls back to the eager path. The eager optimizers in `grokking_optimizers/optimizers/*.py` are **pure PyTorch** (zero `_C`/`torch.ops`/`.apply` calls — verified). **Therefore none of these kernel bugs are reached by the grokking race as currently wired.** They are live on the **Phase-2 kernel-audit path**: `verify_all`, `test_reference_parity`, and any direct `_C` caller. Every item below is "dormant in the race, live in the audit." Ranking tiebreaks blast-radius by failure mode: silent corruption > loud crash/OOB.

All repros assume: `pip install -e . && python -c "import grokking_optimizers._C as c"` first (recompile + import).

---

### P1 — `muon_sm90.cuh:258` — inverted weight-decay (silent catastrophic corruption) — HIGH / certain
- **Issue:** Fused NS-combine+update computes `p + neg_lr_scale*y - decay_factor*p`, retaining `(1−decay_factor)` of the param instead of `decay_factor`. Host passes `decay_factor = 1.0f - lr*wd` (bindings.cpp:970). With defaults lr=0.02, wd=1.0 → retains **2%** of param instead of **98%**. The non-fused `muon_update_kernel` (same file) uses the correct `p*decay_factor`, so the two paths disagree — a bug under any convention.
- **Fix:** `param[i] = static_cast<ParamT>(p * decay_factor + neg_lr_scale * y);`
- **Verify (H100):** one-step numeric assert. Build a 2D param `p=torch.ones(64,64,device='cuda')`, zero NS inputs (`X=AX=AAX=zeros`), call `c.muon_ns_combine_update_fused(p, X, AX, AAX, a=1,b=0,c_=0, neg_lr_scale=0.0, decay_factor=0.98)`, then `assert torch.allclose(p, torch.full_like(p,0.98), atol=1e-3)`. Pre-fix yields ≈0.02 (FAIL); post-fix ≈0.98 (PASS).

## 2. Fork-B decoder TC kernel — agent-a6bd46c6 (READ FULL, L0–L1125) — "THE perf milestone"

Task R2.3 (L0): author the Fork-B (dW-output-stationary) fwd+bwd+AdamW persistent kernel on the
VALIDATED engine. FOUNDATIONS (committed): `wgmma.cuh` + `tile_pipeline.cuh` (18/18);
`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh` engine 13/13 (`tc_gemm_block_unpipelined` all 3 orientations, DecActs
Fork-B layout); GEMM_IMPL seam in `fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh` (=1 currently `#error`s).
CONTRACT = `DESIGN-TC-PIPELINE.md`: bf16 GEMMs fp32-acc; softmax/LN/CE fp32; per-sample attention
stays scalar (seq=4 tiny); embedding owner-scan deterministic; AdamW fused in dW epilogue; no
per-CTA partial buffers; no B1 barrier.

Design realized (L68, L101, L130, L356):
- ~33% of FLOPs each in fwd/dX/dW → all three must go through TCs (M=kTileM=128 = 32 samples × 4
  positions; wgmma needs M≥64, one sample is only 4 rows → tile-batching mandatory).
- Tile activations live in HBM (`DecActs`); smem only holds engine A/B staging tiles. Workspace
  ~298 MB at full B (vs scalar 223 MB) (L100, L1727).
- Weights are fp32 in params, converted to bf16 ON-READ inside the GEMM accessor (no pre-staged
  bf16 weight buffer) (L260, L1725) — this exact decision later BLOCKS the cp.async ring (see §5).
- Phase layout: P0 zero LN-vec/loss; B0; P1 per-tile fwd→bwd (writes DecActs X-inputs + dY
  adjoints + dh0 + LN-vec partials); B1; P2 dW output-stationary (50 dW tiles, owner = tile%nCTA,
  MaxAtomsM=1) + biases + embedding owner-scan + LN-vec reduce; B2; P3 scalar AdamW tail.
- NO asymmetric setmaxnreg (the scalar driver's `reg_dealloc<32>` on wg0 would starve the wgmma
  warpgroup — matched the validated selftest's no-split config) (L65, L375).

THREE BACKWARD BUGS found+fixed during validation (forward was exact from the start — loss
rel 2.5e-4) (L631, L654, L725, L857, L1696–1699):
1. **ff0/in_proj dX Kin/Nout swapped** — ff0 dX was a 4× buffer OVERFLOW into `sc.x1`, trampling
   downstream buffers (advisor-pinpointed) (L654).
2. **dW output-stationary double-counted mbase** — `tc_gemm_block_unpipelined` already passes the
   GLOBAL row `m = mbase+mn` to the accessor; the dW accessor added `mbase` again (`mbase+mbase+mn`)
   → all weight dW wrong (rel ~1.0) while biases (Σ dY) were right (L725). Fix: use `m` raw.
3. **Per-layer LN/qkv/ff0pre/attn caches single-buffered** (the dominant bug) — forward runs ALL
   layers then backward runs ALL layers, so layer-0's bwd read layer-1's overwritten caches →
   classic compounding error (layer-1 grads ~0.05 OK, layer-0 ~0.3–0.95 wrong). Fix: index the
   caches `[li]` per layer (L857).

## 4. ENDGAME #13 cp.async ring — agent-a64c698 (time-boxed; CLEAN REVERT + blocker report)

Target: cp.async producer/consumer mbarrier ring in the decoder TC GEMM engine — "the structural
fix all three prior moves pointed at." Live baseline established: **d=1024 B=16384 = 968.5 ms /
10.23 TF/s / 1.03% MFU** (3 reps 969.0/968.5/967.6). Profile (clock64 critical path): P1_fwd 27.0%
+ P1_bwd 29.4% + P2_dW_GEMM 26.8% + B1_barrier 14.4% (the three GEMM phases ~83%).

OUTCOME: reverted to f78a9e2 cleanly (wiring 33/33); no commit; honest documented failure (per
directive). Two blockers found:

BLOCKER 1 — the d=1024 bench is UNRUNNABLE at HEAD (pre-existing regression, NOT the ring):
`tuning/decoder_bench.py --d 1024 --B 16384` OOMs at workspace alloc ("Tried to allocate 191.97
GiB") before any kernel. Root cause: commit **7656ea6** ("de-pin d=128 SuperGrok2 Nmax constants",
task #24) re-derived `kDecSG2Nmax` = 4d² = 4.19M at d=1024 → `dec_sg2_ws_stride_floats` ≈ 377M
floats/CTA × 132 CTAs ≈ 199 GB, UNCONDITIONALLY carved even for AdamW. Self-documented at
`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:443-455`. Fix found+verified (~35 lines, production-invisible): gate
the 4 staged-opt scratch regions (Prodigy/Muon/LookSAM/SG2) to 0 floats at bench width via
`#if SG_DEC_BENCH_LAYOUT`. Reverted per directive; "next session should re-apply it first."

BLOCKER 2 — the cp.async/mbarrier ring is STRUCTURALLY blocked on this engine (the real finding):
- (a) **fp32 weights converted on-read** (the §2 design decision) — cp.async/TMA copy RAW bytes and
  cannot convert fp32→bf16. In fwd the weight tile is the LARGER operand / dominant HBM traffic and
  must stay synchronous; async-ing only the smaller bf16 A operand has a ceiling ~2-3% (within
  noise → fails "faster beyond noise"). Real fix (pre-staged bf16 weights) needs a new conversion
  phase + cross-CTA buffer + barrier = explicitly out of scope.
- (b) the dW phase (26.8%) has BOTH operands transposed-strided → needs TMA-with-transpose, which
  the design makes phase-2 (`tile_pipeline.cuh:199`).
- (c) the shared `tc_gemm_block_unpipelined` (mamba/decoder/vit) already compiles at "255 registers
  with 2636 B spill stores, 2672 B spill loads" — NO headroom for mbarrier ring state → more spills
  or occupancy=0 → GridBarrier HANG. **Register pressure is the true gating constraint.**
- Recommended next steps: (1) land the OOM fix as its own commit; (2) attack obstacle (c) — reduce
  register pressure first; (3) the only sound ring is pre-staged bf16 weights (new P0.5 phase, needs
  barrier-structure scope escalation) OR TMA descriptors per orientation (phase-2). Multi-hour
  structural efforts, not a single-session hill-climb.

NOTE: the cp.async/mbarrier infra ALREADY EXISTS (`tile_pipeline.cuh` TilePipeline<N,Depth>,
`pipeline_produce_ktile`, `tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16`; `warp_specialize.cuh` Mbarrier; primitives
cp_async_cg_16/ca_4/commit/wait_group) but is silicon-validated only in `wgmma_selftest.cu`, never
wired into the megakernel.
